assumptions.statement: Detailed regulatory controls, road redlines, ownership, municipal utilities, and engineering constraints must be confirmed from official attachments before statutory use.
assumptions.impact: The package can be reviewed as a formal AI submission only for provided official boundaries and submitted design layers; statutory controls still need professional confirmation.

assumptions.statement: The site boundary and three key-area polygons are provisional approximations derived from the official announcement text and approximate areas; official polygons are not yet published.
assumptions.impact: All areas, ratios, and geometry-based conclusions must be recalculated once official boundaries are available; provisional values are for display and discussion only.

assumptions.statement: Existing buildings, ownership, regulatory plans, and engineering conditions are not fully available; retain/renovate/demolish conclusions are conceptual and require field and statutory verification.
assumptions.impact: Building-scale and renewal conclusions remain a verification checklist, not implementation decisions.

assumptions.statement: Road redlines, cross-sections, utility networks, drainage, fire, and municipal data are missing; traffic and municipal proposals are conceptual design directions.
assumptions.impact: Traffic and infrastructure statements cannot be treated as engineering conclusions until data is confirmed.

assumptions.statement: Annual activities, developer community operations, scenario open-call operations, international communication, and investment attraction are conceptual operating directions, not confirmed government commitments.
assumptions.impact: Operating plans are proposals to be tested through public pilots and professional review.

assumptions.statement: AI scenario cards describe directions whose technical maturity, privacy handling, and human-review processes must be validated before any pilot deployment.
assumptions.impact: No scenario is claimed as fully deployable or approved; each requires data-minimization, explainability, and human review.
